2c28d037868ad60da7134f53.title_original: Perceive, Interact, Reason: Building Tool-Augmented Visual Agents for Spatial Reasoning
2c28d037868ad60da7134f53.excerpt: arXiv:2606.12830v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While recent vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate strong multimodal understanding, they remain limited in spatial reasoning tasks that require active evidence acquisition and multi-step visual interaction. This limitation suggests that relying solely on implicit visual representations from vision encoders is insufficient for recovering fine-grained spatial evidence. We introduce PERception-Interaction-reason Agent (PERIA), a tool-augmented visual agent for spatial reasoning tasks across map reasoning, visual probing, and vision reconstruction. PERIA uses two lightweight tool families: vision perception tools for exposing textual, symbolic, and spatial evidence, and vision interaction tools for manipulating visual context, tracing paths, and verifying spatial relations. To train PERIA, we develop a unified recipe that combines supervised tool-use trajectory synthesis, composite rewards, and Observation-Relaxed Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (OR-GIGPO) for effective multi-tool behavior. Experiments on 13 benchmarks from 8 datasets show that PERIA-8B improves over the Qwen3-8B backbone by 10.0 percentage points on in-distribution benchmarks and 4.4 percentage points on out-of-distribution benchmarks, while outperforming previous state-of-the-art baselines of similar size by 6.9--14.8 percentage points. It also achieves performance comparable to much larger models such as Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking and GPT-5, dem

e46a537863838c1a38ef2ed2.title_original: SDS-LoRA: Overcoming Anisotropic Gradient Scaling in Low-Rank Adaptation
e46a537863838c1a38ef2ed2.excerpt: arXiv:2606.16454v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) enables efficient adaptation of large pretrained models to downstream tasks by parameterizing weight updates with low-rank matrices. In this paper, we investigate the limitations of the LoRA parameterization from a geometric perspective. Specifically, we show that when a full fine-tuning gradient is backpropagated to the low-rank matrices, it undergoes anisotropic scaling driven by their singular values. We argue that this phenomenon is undesirable because it distorts the full fine-tuning gradient by skewing it toward dominant singular directions while suppressing others. Our analyses demonstrate that anisotropic gradient scaling reduces the effective rank of the low-rank matrices' gradients and fails to provide the best possible alignment between the full fine-tuning gradient and its low-rank approximation in LoRA for arbitrary gradients, thereby exacerbating the gap to full fine-tuning. To address these limitations, we propose a new low-rank parameterization, SDS-LoRA, which Structurally Decouples Singular values from the backward pass. Our method ensures that the full fine-tuning gradient backpropagates only through the orthonormal bases of the low-rank matrices' subspaces, independent of their scales. Convergence analysis demonstrates that while LoRA's convergence rate degrades with the condition number of the low-rank matrices, that of SDS-LoRA remains independent of it. Experimental res

1e4688e103f92c67b09a8b14.title_original: Descriptor: Certus Caliber Classification Gunshot Dataset (C3GD)
1e4688e103f92c67b09a8b14.excerpt: arXiv:2606.18135v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we introduce the Certus Caliber Classification Gunshot Dataset (C3GD), a publicly accessible dataset developed for the analysis of firearm muzzle blast sounds. The dataset aims to provide a wide variety of firearms, calibers, cartridges, microphones, and microphone locations with metadata detailed beyond what is currently available. It comprises more than 12,000 live-fire data points from 45 firearms across 18 calibers, including nine calibers not present in existing datasets. Live-fire data collection in semi-controlled environments is costly, but using internet-collected data increases the risk of low-quality data and label noise. This dataset focuses primarily on caliber classification, but can also facilitate gunshot detection, audio separation, and audio signal processing applications, providing a diverse and realistic reference. It aims to provide enough diversity to generalize to live-fire applications while also providing enough metadata for detailed academic analysis.

e3e9ef44fdf9c17a0cf6f564.title_original: MotionHalluc: Diagnosing Kinematic Hallucinations in Fine-Grained Motion Reasoning
e3e9ef44fdf9c17a0cf6f564.excerpt: arXiv:2606.23061v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motion instruction generation in cross-video comparison aims to produce corrective feedback that describes the differences between a query and a reference motion. However, existing models often generate instructions that exhibit motion hallucinations, failing to reflect actual kinematic differences between paired videos. To systematically investigate these hallucinations, we introduce MotionHalluc, a dedicated benchmark for evaluating motion hallucinations in paired-video comparison. MotionHalluc comprises 1540 fine-grained questions over 553 video pairs, evaluating hallucinations along three core dimensions: (1)directional hallucination, (2)attributional hallucination, and (3)temporal hallucination. Extensive evaluations of state-of-the-art large multimodal models demonstrate high susceptibility to these hallucinations. Furthermore, we provide Perceive-Parse-Verify (PPV) as a training-free measurements extraction and verification baseline that converts candidate instructions into executable measurement queries and supplies kinematic measurements at inference time. Our results show that this simple measurements injection yields an average 10.6% performance gain across models, suggesting that motion reasoning with explicit quantitative measurements is a key factor in reducing hallucinations in cross-video comparison. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Leocoding0971/MotionHalluc.

0f3f7aadf3596f677c579dcd.title_original: ReactiveBFM: Reactive Closed-Loop Motion Planning Towards Universal Humanoid Whole-Body Control
0f3f7aadf3596f677c579dcd.excerpt: arXiv:2606.30362v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While current Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) provide robust control priors for humanoids, they only execute pre-defined reference motions. As a result, they are vulnerable to environmental shifts and incapable of reactive whole-body coordination. Naively cascading them with generative motion planners fails to achieve true reactivity, as inevitable tracking discrepancies induce fatal cumulative exposure bias. To bridge this gap, we propose ReactiveBFM, a real-time closed-loop planning-control framework. At its core, we effectively mitigate exposure bias via a scheduled prefix sampling curriculum, forcing the generative planner to actively learn error-recovery behaviors from imperfect physical states rather than ground-truth trajectories. Systematically, to reconcile the severe latency mismatch between auto-regressive planning and high-frequency tracking, we introduce an asynchronous replanning mechanism. Combined with trajectory chunking to temporally ensemble spatial references, our system guarantees spatio-temporally fluid execution without physical jitter. Deployed on the Unitree G1 humanoid, ReactiveBFM demonstrates unprecedented physical agility across a vast repertoire of text-conditioned closed-loop motions. Notably, ReactiveBFM achieves zero-shot moving target reaching, showcasing intricate whole-body coordination and on-the-fly replanning. e388a5b4c6636a0d355b1fad.title_original: PosterHarness: Turning Scientific Poster Generation into an Auditable Instruction-Following Benchmark
e388a5b4c6636a0d355b1fad.excerpt: arXiv:2607.03006v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Text-rich image models can now design poster-scale layouts, but we lack ways to measure whether they honor scientific communication contracts: legible labels, prescribed aspect ratios, and -- above all -- abstaining from fabricated scientific figures. We present POSTERHARNESS, an auditable harness reframing poster generation as measurable instruction-following tasks, with a pilot benchmark and failure taxonomy. POSTERHARNESS uses a placeholder-first contract to separate two jobs models otherwise conflate. The model performs visual-summary design: typography, reading path, color, and background -- but never draws data-bearing figures. Every figure region must be an empty labeled placeholder; a deterministic compositor inserts real source-paper figures at detected coordinates. This makes properties measurable: placeholder count and ID accuracy, blankness, aspect-ratio compliance, abstention from synthesized graphics, public-text hygiene, and source-figure provenance -- with failures logged as explicit rejections, not hidden in plausible-looking output. We instantiate the harness on 12 papers (6 HEP, 6 AI/ML-adjacent) and report three findings. (i) A counterfactual probe shows the placeholder contract drives VLM-counted synthesized figures from 34 to 0 across three papers. b59abb5c2c56ff451ce5731c.title_original: Robustness Verification of an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle-based Plankton Classifier
b59abb5c2c56ff451ce5731c.excerpt: arXiv:2607.04453v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The assessment of planktonic standing stocks and microorganism structures is critical for understanding upper ocean biological processes. Currently, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) equipped with in-situ optical imaging and artificial intelligence (AI) methods offer a promising solution for persistent surveillance, mapping and monitoring of planktonic life. However, current AI methods often lack robustness in dynamic, unstructured environments, where environmental noise and non-biological artifacts lead to frequent misclassifications. Standard convolutional neural network (CNN) classifiers often struggle with such conditions, leading to misclassifications that require time-consuming manual validation by marine biologists. To address this issue, we propose a novel robustness verification framework for in-situ plankton classifiers based on reachability analysis. We also introduce a continuous-time neural ordinary differential equation (neural ODE) classification model leveraging the high-resolution imaging capabilities of the SilCam particle imager. In this paper, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework by formally verifying the robustness of the neural ODE model against environmental perturbations. We demonstrate that our verification framework acts as an automated filter providing formal guarantees of model stability against ambiguous data, thereby improving the reliability of autonomous samplin

8b90aad2377c791b18c30283.title_original: AirPASS: Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Pinching Antenna Systems
8b90aad2377c791b18c30283.excerpt: arXiv:2607.06768v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates over-the-air federated learning (AirFL) in wireless systems where the access point is equipped with a multi-waveguide pinching antenna system (PASS). We adopt the widely studied learning-oriented AirFL formulation, which seeks to maximize the number of selected devices while keeping the aggregation distortion below a prescribed threshold. The resulting joint optimization of device selection, receive beamforming, and pinching-antenna placement is highly nonconvex due to the intricate coupling among these system variables. To address this challenge, we develop AirPASS, an alternating optimization framework with two main components: a homotopy-Riemannian margin-consolidation method for device selection and receive beamforming under a fixed PASS configuration, and a homotopy-assisted geometry optimization method for updating the pinching-antenna positions under fixed selected devices and beamformer.

8f938be12877aea3bca01a46.title_original: Context-Aware Subtitle Translation on CPU: Deployment-Driven Training, Evaluation, and Latency Design
8f938be12877aea3bca01a46.excerpt: arXiv:2607.09957v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study English-to-Traditional-Chinese (Taiwan) subtitle translation for a free browser extension, where the model must run on the viewer's CPU in about 500 ms per subtitle. We train two models built on the LMT-60 base models, Sotto-1.7B and the deployed Sotto-0.6B, with a task-specific vocabulary, continued pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, weight interpolation, logit distillation and on-policy preference optimization. Because reference translations of subtitles are unreliable, we evaluate by pairwise comparison against one fixed baseline, Google Translate, with each pair judged in both orders by a panel of two LLM judges. On 1,820 held-out subtitles, Sotto-1.7B has a win rate of 0.576 against the baseline and wins head-to-head against four open translation models, and is slightly below a 27B model. We split latency into prefill and decoding: idle-time prefill, which prefills the known part of the prompt while waiting for the next subtitle, cuts mean end-to-end latency by 31% on a CPU, and the task-specific vocabulary encodes the same Chinese text in 28% fewer tokens. The deployed model stays within 500 ms for every subtitle in our latency test. The code is available at https://github.com/aiden1020/localsubs .

634780419c465169e968ec51.title_original: WhisperRec: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models
634780419c465169e968ec51.excerpt: arXiv:2607.26621v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong reasoning capabilities, motivating their adoption as backbones for foundation recommendation models (FRMs). Existing approaches typically enhance recommendation with explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) under the Think-then-Answer paradigm. However, generating lengthy rationales introduces substantial inference overhead, while fixed CoT templates struggle to model diverse, dynamic, and context-dependent user interests. We propose WhisperRec, an efficient latent reasoning framework for FRMs. WhisperRec compresses teacher-generated CoT into learnable latent reasoning tokens, enabling a Latent-Reason-then-Answer paradigm that performs reasoning in latent space without producing verbose rationales. This design retains decision-relevant reasoning information while avoiding the latency bottleneck of autoregressive rationale generation. Specifically, it first introduces Multi-View Adaptive CoT (MV-ACoT) to construct diverse, high-quality supervision from complementary perspectives on user interests. MV-ACoT also adapts reasoning complexity to each instance, applying lightweight analysis to clear cases and targeted multi-factor reasoning to challenging ones. Building on a pre-trained FRM, WhisperRec then employs a three-stage Latent Reasoning Alignment procedure to progressively internalize teacher CoT into latent representations. 122d1f1c5fb20415c7488328.title_original: ARES: Adaptive Reasoning-Effort Steering for PPA- and Cost-Aware RTL Optimization with LLM Agents
122d1f1c5fb20415c7488328.excerpt: arXiv:2607.27879v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents optimize the power, performance, and area (PPA) of register-transfer-level (RTL) designs by iterating over edits, synthesis, and PPA analysis, paying a dollar cost for every LLM call. Prior agents report the quality reached without its normalized cost, attribute that quality to an engineered cross-design memory, and hold the reasoning effort of every call fixed. We propose Ares with three corresponding innovations. (1) We introduce a normalized dollar cost per LLM call reported alongside the figure of merit (FoM), enabling fair comparison across effort levels and optimizers. (2) Using this accounting, we find the construction of the long-term memory matters little. An engineered memory brings no dependable gain over a plain concatenation of the same experience. (3) We instead adapt the per-call reasoning effort by escalating to deeper reasoning only once progress at a lower effort stalls, via a patience counter fit on 21 training designs, allocating reasoning where it pays rather than uniformly across all iterations. On three test designs unseen during training, the effort policy lowers the FoM by 22-28% with Opus 4.6 and by 18-34% with GPT-5.5, where the best fixed effort reaches 20-24% and 19-29%, respectively, at equal normalized cost. Ares closes on average 91% of the gap from an LLM-drafted multiply-accumulate unit to its highly hand-optimized counterpart. It also reaches a 5% low

9d6017062e9288818ad16eac.title_original: TORUS: A Unified Closed-Loop Benchmark for Unified Audio Models
9d6017062e9288818ad16eac.excerpt: arXiv:2607.28896v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Unified audio models capable of audio understanding, audio generation and, increasingly, audio editing are proliferating rapidly. However, each capability is evaluated in isolation on specialized benchmarks and a basic question remains unanswered: can these models understand the audio they generate/edit i.e. do they exhibit audio understanding-generation self-coherence (UGC_OWN)? We introduce TORUS, an audio-native unified benchmark for holistic, closed-loop evaluation of unified audio models comprising 1,053 questions (117 tests) spanning 21 tasks and 8 audio domain settings across all 3 audio types. We evaluate unified models and cascades of specialized models across objective and subjective metrics. Best unified models are able to answer only 52.4% questions about their generations, while gpt-audio can answer 53.6% questions. We hypothesize that a truly unified audio intelligence should be highly self-coherent and thus position understanding-generation coherence as an essential test for future unified audio systems. Further details are on our project page: https://torus-benchmark.github.io/

0df470b3483bdde8f07dd8e7.excerpt: arXiv:2608.03496v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Autonomous robots are moving rapidly from research labs into everyday life - on roads, in the air, in warehouses, and in space. Robot autonomy is no longer solely an academic pursuit, but a collection of mature, field-tested methods and tools that practitioners rely on in real-world deployments. This book offers a clear, unified introduction to the methods that make this possible. Built on decades of teaching at Stanford, the text develops the core elements of modern autonomy stacks within a single conceptual framework, bridging classical robotics and modern physical AI. Every major topic is paired with hands-on Jupyter notebooks and implementation-driven exercises, so readers build practical intuition alongside theoretical understanding. The result is a principled, accessible, and deployment-aware foundation for anyone seeking to design, analyze, or contribute to the next generation of autonomous systems. This is a comprehensive resource for students, engineers, and researchers entering one of today's fastest-growing fields.

879dd5c04f3de9a5cd220b3a.title_original: Beyond Naturalness: Probing Automated Text-To-Speech Evaluators on Linguistically Grounded Dimensions
879dd5c04f3de9a5cd220b3a.excerpt: arXiv:2608.09930v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automated Text-to-Speech (TTS) evaluation methods (Mean Opinion Score (MOS) predictors and Audio Large Language Model (Audio-LLM) judges) are expected to reflect human perception, yet it is unclear how well they capture the distinct aspects of speech that listeners actually perceive. We deconstruct "naturalness" into a linguistically grounded annotation schema spanning 10 distinct perceptual dimensions, and use it to construct the first dimension-level meta-evaluation benchmark for TTS, comprising 860 utterances annotated by trained linguist raters. Results from benchmarking four MOS predictors and four Audio-LLM judges reveal that MOS predictors are more sensitive to acoustic signal-level properties at the prosodic and paralinguistic levels, while Audio-LLM judges show selective, prompt-dependent detection that favors word-level errors and does not generalize across all dimensions. Neither class reliably captures a breadth of linguistically structured, human-perceptible speech errors. Our dataset, annotation schema, and evaluation code are publicly released to support more targeted and interpretable TTS evaluation.

4274dccab19c3e3980acf8d3.title_original: Mimir: A Sub-2B Hierarchical Reasoning Model Trained on Permissible Data Punches Above Its Weight Class
4274dccab19c3e3980acf8d3.excerpt: arXiv:2608.13517v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Training capable language models typically relies on web-scale pretraining followed by multi-stage post-training, creating substantial computational and data-governance barriers for settings in which training data must satisfy explicit permissibility constraints. We introduce Mimir, a 1.78B-parameter language model based on the Hierarchical Reasoning Model Text (HRM-Text) architecture, a recurrent-depth transformer whose layers are split into a low-level (L) and a high-level (H) stack that are applied repeatedly in an interleaved schedule. Mimir is trained from random initialization directly on a curated mixture of instruction, reasoning, tool-use, multilingual, and synthetic data: 161 datasets and 70.5B tokens per epoch for Mimir v1, extended to 103B tokens per epoch for its continued-training successor Mimir v1.5, with synthetic replacements for sources that do not satisfy permissibility criteria. Across 20 benchmarks in English, Danish (a low-resource language with ~6M speakers), and Math & Code, Mimir v1.5 attains the highest average score of all sub-2B models in every domain, outperforming both HRM-Text 1B and the looped transformers Ouro 1.4B and Ouro 2.6B, and Mimir matches or exceeds the performance of models of up to 9B parameters, such as Qwen 3.5 9B and Gemma 4 E4B, on the English and Danish averages. Two independent memorisation audits indicate low memorisation risk despite multi-epoch training. Inference-t

185a474c58a589408d1ec97d.title_original: Interrupting the Loop: Periodic Subject Changes Raise Judged Surprise and Connection in Base Language Models
185a474c58a589408d1ec97d.excerpt: arXiv:2608.19893v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Where does the novelty a base language model produces with no task come from, and what can an LLM judge of a long stream actually see? We dismantle a cognitively inspired generation loop over 24 conditions on three base models. Most of its effect lives in one operation: a new subject injected every few hundred tokens (an interruption) into a stream whose literal repetition is damped (habituation). We judge windows of generated text only, with the premise as the unit (n=10) and a judge measured for repeatability, against a second judge family and human readers. Under that protocol the interruption raises judged surprise by 1.2 to 1.4 points and connection by 0.7 to 0.9 over habituation alone. A connective that asks for continuity hurts; a bare paragraph break adds nothing detectable; a reset context does at least as well as a kept one; and a pre-registered replication on new premises confirms the primary contrast. Three things the window judge could not see changed the first version of this study. The judge scores the experimenter's injected sentence as the model's own. A fixed rotation of injected sentences makes the model replay its own earlier segments (65-80% of post-interruption windows at periods 150-300 are mostly verbatim replay), and the judge scores the replay as surprise and, above all, as connection; at period 300 the source of 62% of windows lies beyond the judge's 600-token horizon. 4e2471e65672187e2701acbb.title_original: Moving the Mean Toward the Known Good, Not Beyond It: What Inference-Time Interventions and Weight Consolidation Buy in Open-Ended Generation
4e2471e65672187e2701acbb.excerpt: arXiv:2608.28886v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: What does a generation loop gain from learning on its own verified successes? A confirmation battery replicates the whole procedure three times, with fresh seeds and a never-consulted held-out set read exactly once: the mean was nearly identical in all three lineages (-2.0, -1.8, -1.9), and after aggregating within held-out variant all seven evaluable variants favored consolidation (p=0.008). The best observed candidate moved to the classic heuristic's level, exactly (0.021028, the lowest variant's classic level, in all three lineages and both arms); attract never went beyond its variant's classic level, while the random control did in 7 of 24 lineage-variant cells. A matched SFT-only control shows the supervised anchor, not repulsion from bad candidates, does the concentrating (96% of candidates land exactly at the classic heuristic's level). c3697e0f00ecc7db9a405ea1.title_original: FluxVLA Engine: A One-Stop VLA Engineering Platform for Embodied Intelligence
c3697e0f00ecc7db9a405ea1.excerpt: arXiv:2609.17210v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models, world-action models (WAMs), and offline reinforcement learning methods are rapidly expanding the design space of embodied policies, yet turning these algorithms into reliable robot systems remains constrained by fragmented data formats, training stacks, evaluation protocols, inference runtimes, and embodiment-specific interfaces. We present $\mathrm{FluxVLA}$ Engine, an open, configuration-driven platform that turns heterogeneous embodied-policy components into a reproducible data-to-deployment workflow. Rather than introducing another policy model, $\mathrm{FluxVLA}$ standardizes interfaces for datasets, visual-language and world models, action heads, reward- or advantage-weighted learning, distributed training, simulation evaluation, optimized inference, and robot operators. The engine further integrates compositional dual-arm simulation, scalable automatic data generation, and model-decoupled human-in-the-loop rollout, takeover, correction collection, and reward annotation. For responsive physical execution, it combines Real-Time Chunking (RTC) with accelerated inference backends, lightweight remote GPU serving, and configurable trajectory post-processing. Together, these capabilities connect offline learning, simulation validation, online correction, and real-robot execution through shared and auditable contracts. $\mathrm{FluxVLA}$ therefore targets the engineering bottlenecks

36b1d13ccf6ad321863c00f0.title_original: Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation with Imperfect Teachers
36b1d13ccf6ad321863c00f0.excerpt: arXiv:2609.18321v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Offline on-policy distillation gains efficiency by collecting student trajectories and teacher supervision once and reusing them throughout optimization. The same reuse makes imperfect supervision persistent. Since even strong teachers can fail, we ask \emph{what remains learnable from imperfect teacher supervision?} Teacher failure is only a coarse problem-level signal and does not imply that all supervision along the associated student trajectory is unhelpful. A natural alternative is to estimate teacher recoverability along the trajectory, but repeated continuations largely erase the efficiency advantage of offline distillation. We instead use teacher-successful problems to define a cheap reference for what the student can learn. We train on teacher-successful problems and measure how the likelihood of each observed token in trajectories from teacher-failed problems changes. We use these signed likelihood changes as an operational \emph{learnability signal}: larger increases indicate behavior more strongly promoted by successful-only learning. We aggregate this signal into trajectory-level weights for the original distillation loss. Unlike continuation-based estimates, our learnability requires no additional generation and can be computed once from stored trajectories and model checkpoints. c30a870b85f6127524cc661c.title_original: Initial Evaluation of Potential Bias in Coverage of Humans in Wikidata
c30a870b85f6127524cc661c.excerpt: arXiv:2609.22375v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Introduction. Open collaborative knowledge graphs such as Wikidata increasingly ground agentic artificial intelligence, information retrieval, and language modeling systems, making systematic auditing of their demographic representation and overall equity a research imperative. Methods. Herein, we present an open-source auditing platform that ingests over 10 million statement bindings representing over 6 million humans on Wikidata via QLever, and evaluates representation of gender, sexual orientation, geography, birthplace urbanicity, ethnicity, multilingual coverage of labels, descriptions, and aliases, occupation, and select intersectional pairs of these entities. It does so by making use of Chi-square goodness-of-fit tests, 95% Wilson-score confidence intervals, and disparity ratios, in light of Rubin's missingness taxonomy. Results. Women accounted for 28.71% (CI +/-0.04) of all humans in Wikidata with a stated gender. 38.26% of humans had a citizenship statement, with Western Europe and North America (WENA) representing approximately 53% of such statements. Among 1.8 million birthplaces that could be classified, rural birthplaces were observed in 2.48% of cases (in comparison to 27.4% global baseline). Fewer than 1.2% of entities carried an ethnicity statement, and non-English Wikidata descriptions covered 18.2% of items. Discussion. Our findings reveal significant missingness across the evaluated axes. Ethnicity

cc07ccf41ee8cef2708bc738.title_original: The Price of Safety: Benign-Case Utility and Token Overhead of Memory-Poisoning Defenses in LLM Agents
cc07ccf41ee8cef2708bc738.excerpt: arXiv:2609.22818v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Memory-poisoning defenses for LLM agents are typically evaluated by how well they stop attacks, even though almost all traffic they encounter is benign. We measure their cost when no attack is present. Our harness holds the memory backend, retrieval, answer prompt, and judge constant, changing only the defense. We test four defenses on half of LoCoMo: five long conversations with 750 turns and 255 questions per run, repeated three times each. Replication proved necessary: one run showed a reranker cost on adversarial questions that the other two did not. The three write-time defenses (sanitization, provenance checking, and LLM-based anomaly detection) never fired on benign traffic. cafede4ca45dccaf9912a12a.title_original: FlashBoB: I/O-Efficient Exact Backward-over-Backward for Softmax Attention
cafede4ca45dccaf9912a12a.excerpt: arXiv:2609.24089v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Transformer models built on the attention mechanism have become a central building block in modern deep learning, yet softmax attention remains a major bottleneck for long-context workloads. The key insight is a hierarchical affine structure in the softmax double backward: two row-wise scalars determine all outputs through affine transformations. This yields a two-pass schedule with bounded on-chip static random-access memory (SRAM) usage and minimal off-chip high-bandwidth memory (HBM) traffic. 8ff3f0b0ecbff323398babba.excerpt: arXiv:2609.29636v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Verified search, in which a language model proposes programs, a hard evaluator scores them, and selection keeps the best, has recently moved mathematical records; controlled ablations of the proposer-side components remain rare. The factorial finds no positive memory-by-repulsion interaction (bounded to about +/-0.04); the gain decomposes additively, and memory+repulsion is the only arm that never collapses (0 of 18 runs), within 0.025 of the full composition. 6dd7045fa8752e498423d6d3.title_original: CollabFlow: Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Collaboration
6dd7045fa8752e498423d6d3.excerpt: arXiv:2609.38662v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) lets a system improve from its own outcomes; in LLM-based multi-agent systems, Agents refine one another within a task, and outcomes improve how they collaborate across tasks. However, existing multi-agent collaboration leaves this loop open: collaboration is pre-defined at the operator level, topology-only learning keeps verbatim exchange that propagates errors, and reward maximization on a system's own outcomes concentrates on a few teams. To address these challenges, we propose CollabFlow, an RSI system of Learned Agent Collaboration: a trainable Collab-Director constructs teams of complete Agents, a frozen executor runs them, and each round's outcomes retrain the director. Within each round, the edges of a collaboration graph carry protocols of Evidence-Conditioned Communication: a receiver adopts a differing answer only when the sender's evidence is stronger by a margin, so the director learns who communicates and how. Across rounds, we further propose Collaborative Trajectory Balance (CTB), a flow-based objective that credits each team once across its construction orders and targets a reward-proportional distribution over teams, so several good teams stay in play. We also bound how far this self-generated target moves between rounds, which shrinks as records accumulate. On twelve datasets, CollabFlow outperforms all baselines and keeps improving across rounds. 9c2a26cae38da127e12b97c3.title_original: Scale and Selection: What Makes Automatic Harness Evolution Work for Visual-Interface Robot Agents
9c2a26cae38da127e12b97c3.excerpt: arXiv:2609.39304v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When an off-the-shelf coding agent is used directly as a robot policy, observing a browser-based 3D interface through screenshots and acting by posing a virtual target gripper through a few tools, the agent's harness, its prompts, tools, and control rules, largely determines success, and until now it has been written by hand. We show that this harness can be improved automatically by another coding agent, the optimizer agent, and report two findings about what makes it work. First, the number of rollouts the optimizer agent sees per round governs whether the evolved harness generalizes: with rounds fixed, held-out success rises as the training batch grows from 5 to 100 rollouts, while small batches overfit the training tasks. Second, the optimizer agent must not be given free rein. Accepting every revision it proposes degrades the harness within a few rounds; a simple Champion-Challenger rule that promotes a revision only if it beats the incumbent on the same fixed cases turns the same loop into one that raises held-out success on LIBERO tasks from 51% to 67% over 30 rounds. The evolved harness is also a natural place to attach a pretrained policy, through one tool that hands it control. f713710c62ea3c934494a0a1.title_original: PACT: End-to-End Learning of Human Pose, Contacts, and Forces from Video
f713710c62ea3c934494a0a1.excerpt: arXiv:2610.00451v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Human motion, environmental contacts, and interaction forces are governed by common physical laws, yet existing approaches typically separate visual pose reconstruction from contact and force estimation. This separation limits joint reasoning and can propagate errors between stages. Our approach augments a human reconstruction foundation model with learnable contact-force tokens and a temporal transformer that integrates visual features with world-space motion. Joint prediction heads refine human poses and estimate contacts and forces, while physics-based supervision encourages consistency between the reconstructed motion and interaction forces. To address the scarcity of force annotations, we develop a data annotation pipeline that combines contact labeling with physics-based motion and force optimization, producing training supervision from synthetic and real-world videos. We also introduce a real-world climbing benchmark ForceWall with climbing videos and corresponding ground-truth contact forces obtained from the force sensors. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art contact and force estimation, outperforming staged reconstruction approaches and generalizing to interactions beyond the training distribution. These results support end-to-end joint learning as an effective approach to

6a257e3f018a1dcfe2759bea.title_original: Where Polanyi Meets Galois: Tacit Knowing as an Algebro-Deterministic Operation, Toward Re-rooting AI-Generated Science
6a257e3f018a1dcfe2759bea.excerpt: arXiv:2610.16102v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We argue that tacit knowing is better modelled as an operating regime of a memory than as a kind of content. This audit-valuation complementarity formalizes Polanyi's claim that tacit and explicit are not sharply divided. It separates contingent tacitness, which a new query brings out (AlphaGo's game tree), from regime-bound tacitness, statable only once it is gone (AlphaGo's hunches). (1) Polanyi's from-to structure reads as non-commutative binding. (2) Explicating the valuation destroys it, as with Polanyi's pianist, yet a closed-form law states it. Polanyi, Nonaka, Tsoukas and Collins each capture part of this, narrowly; even Nonaka and von Krogh's continuum cannot tell the classes apart. (3) Collins's three tacit knowledges become strata, one outside the substrate. (4) Our mentor-student DAG is a tacit-transmission graph. (5) Tao's remark that AI-solved problems spawn few follow-ups reveals rootless explicit knowledge: checkable results no one can trace or yet understands. 6afdba2558b0810c3ccb50b4.title_original: Beyond LLM Judge: Mechanical Verification for Agentic Autoformalization
6afdba2558b0810c3ccb50b4.excerpt: arXiv:2610.20573v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a novel method for verifying Lean formalizations that goes beyond LLM-judged faithfulness. Unlike most verification methods, which rely on LLMs or trained models, our method combines LLM-based semantic review with mechanical numerical and vacuity checks, providing checkable feedback and detecting errors missed by LLM judges. We apply this method, along with our Extract-Verify-Proof autoformalization pipeline, to construct the Formalized Library of Mathematical Functions (FLMF), a partial formalization of the NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions (DLMF). On three labeled datasets, our method achieves the lowest accepted-error rate among the evaluated methods, measured as the fraction of incorrect statements accepted by the verification method. Expert review of the results also identifies translation and source defects in existing datasets. Code available at https://github.com/annamei1/FLMF-Ch7ErrFunc-Release.git.

fea1af6ba99a5f8a90440855.title_original: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction
fea1af6ba99a5f8a90440855.excerpt: arXiv:2610.20731v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Humans interpret multimodal observations of the world and forecast how it will evolve. Recent multimodal generative systems have demonstrated similar capabilities: they can integrate multimodal context and synthesize visual outputs that depict changes in the world. To characterize this emerging trajectory, we organize model capabilities into a four-level hierarchy and discover that higher-level tasks remain relatively underexplored despite model progress. To bridge this gap, we explore model performance on multi-step world state prediction, a high-level task that requires models to forecast successive future world states from multimodal observations and diverse references. Such a task requires models to possess entangled understanding and generation capabilities, as well as extensive world knowledge to translate human action sequences, physical transformations, and abstract visual reasoning into coherent visual outputs. We introduce WorldCast, a benchmark comprising 320 manually designed cases across eight categories, and evaluate 12 representative models. The conducted experiments yield three key insights: (a) advances in frontier models are rapidly pushing the boundaries of intelligent world modeling, with the GPT-Image-2.5 System scoring 72.8 and demonstrating early-stage visual state prediction capabilities on real-world tasks; (b) WorldCast reveals substantial gaps between models: even Nano Banana Pro reaches only

947199dfb6594da96561388c.title_original: Qwen-Audio-Jev: A Unified Interface for Audio Decisions
947199dfb6594da96561388c.excerpt: arXiv:2610.21614v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large audio language models (LALMs) have made substantial progress in audio understanding. However, autoregressive text generation introduces computational overhead and latency in high-throughput applications that require frequent selection, judgment, and scoring. To address this limitation, we introduce Qwen-Audio-Jev, which augments Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR-Flash-Next with a dedicated Jev decision head. The model unifies selection, binary judgment, and scoring through three decision primitives: CHOICE, NOUL, and SCORE. Given an audio input, a natural-language question, and an explicit answer specification, Qwen-Audio-Jev directly outputs a task-conditioned probability distribution or a numerical score through typed decision readouts. Evaluation across 18 benchmarks demonstrates the model's effectiveness: CHOICE achieves 78.40 percent accuracy on MMAU and 83.14 percent on MMSU; NOUL achieves 93.76 percent accuracy on the VoxCeleb1-O speaker verification benchmark; and SCORE achieves a normalized mean absolute error of 0.1235 on NISQA overall quality assessment. These results highlight the potential of Qwen-Audio-Jev for efficient audio decision-making in applications such as large-scale audio screening, speaker verification, and automated quality assessment.

2f495045e8bc72fa18f1c3c8.title_original: When EVM Defaults Break: Three SDK Patterns for UTXO-Family Wallets
2f495045e8bc72fa18f1c3c8.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mainstream Web3 SDKs (e.g., ethers.js, viem) bundle three coupled assumptions: an account-based ledger, a single secp256k1 signer, and input-selection-free transaction construction. These assumptions fail once a chain adopts an extended-UTXO model (here, the Cell model on Nervos CKB), and once the wallet population spans heterogeneous cryptographic primitives (secp256k1, WebAuthn, Schnorr). Using CKBers' Codebase (CCC), a TypeScript SDK, this retrospective case study extracts three recurring patterns from release history and exported APIs: a Transaction Composer that makes capacity-aware input completion and fee estimation declarative, a Unified Signer Abstraction that normalizes signing across heterogeneous wallets behind one interface, and a Connector UI component that ships per-wallet onboarding as a drop-in. The contribution is the articulation of these patterns as transferable design lessons for SDKs targeting UTXO-family ledgers and heterogeneous wallet populations.

61161d32b0394423f30c246b.title_original: Protection Is Not One Event: A Survey of RAG Protection Research by Measured Endpoint
61161d32b0394423f30c246b.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems face security, privacy, and copyright risks including content leakage, source reconstruction, unauthorized access, data poisoning, and prompt injection. Yet RAG protection studies use incompatible evaluation metrics, datasets, and threat models. We present a systematic survey and human-coded evidence map of 118 full-text-confirmed RAG defense papers, organized by measured endpoint rather than claimed goal or defense mechanism. Our seven-family taxonomy covers content disclosure, formal privacy proxies, access control and suppression, corpus-use detection, and pipeline integrity and attribution. Thirty-two annotators double-coded the papers kappa=0.867. The survey identifies three gaps. First, retrieval reranking and context rewriting each span five or six endpoint families, so mechanisms do not identify protection outcomes. Second, only 17.8% of studies use content disclosure or reconstruction as their primary endpoint; under the frozen copyright/ownership relation label, 73.3% of records have corpus-use detection as their primary endpoint, and none have an emitted-expression primary endpoint. Third, most evaluations use general-purpose question-answering datasets and non-adaptive attacks rather than sensitive data and adaptive, multi-turn extraction. ba1ab27ebf6203fac88d4399.title_original: Parameters efficient language model with latent cross-attention for IoT intrusion detection
ba1ab27ebf6203fac88d4399.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models have shown strong potential for intrusion detection, but their high memory and computational demands make them difficult to deploy in resource-constrained IoT environments. In this work, we propose a compact Transformer-based architecture that compresses the input into a small latent space before processing it with a minimal Transformer core. We analyze nine compression configurations, compare parameter sharing with layer stacking, and evaluate our approach against SecurityBERT on two IoT intrusion detection datasets, Edge-IIoTset and CICIoT2023. With only 306k non-embedding parameters and 1.6M parameters in total (6MB), our model is about 7x smaller than SecurityBERT (11.2M parameters, 45MB). With the same privacy-preserving encoding, it outperforms SecurityBERT by about 2 points of macro F1-score on Edge-IIoTset and is within 0.7 points on CICIoT2023. It is also about 89x faster on a simulated edge device. We further show that a single Transformer layer is sufficient, and that parameter sharing matches layer stacking with up to 66% fewer parameters. These findings show that lightweight Transformer-based architectures can provide a practical and accurate solution for intrusion detection in resource-constrained IoT settings

2412109f4c20bedce51e0b82.title_original: PhishGen: Understanding LLM Capabilities in Automated Phishing Website Generation
2412109f4c20bedce51e0b82.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phishing relies on visual deception, traditionally requiring web-development skills or pre-built kits. LLMs erode this barrier by generating functional websites from natural-language prompts, yet prior work does not answer how far LLM-driven generation actually reaches: functionality is assessed by inspection rather than execution; visual fidelity is scored by automated metrics or a few internal coders rather than the humans such pages aim to deceive; evaluation is confined to commercial models; and no study benchmarks generated pages against phishing kits deployed in the wild. We present PhishGen, a framework that evaluates the appearance fidelity and end-to-end functionality of LLM-generated phishing pages. PhishGen constructs prompts across three input modalities in seven combinations with twelve safeguard-bypassing rewriting strategies, generates pages using 14 LLMs spanning commercial, open-source, and uncensored categories, and assesses each via automated similarity metrics, reference-based detectors, a crowdsourced user study, and execution-based functionality testing, benchmarking all results against 64 real-world phishing kits. 09a9b8299f932dd181362106.title_original: Mirage: Targeted Jailbreaks Against Post-Generation Safety Checkers in Multimodal Diffusion Models
09a9b8299f932dd181362106.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-generation safety checkers are widely employed in diffusion-model pipelines to prevent unsafe generated content from reaching users. In this paper, we show that these safety checkers can still be bypassed by our proposed multimodal jailbreak attack, Mirage. Given an adversarial target, which can be either a reference NSFW image or a malicious text description, Mirage conceals the target within an imperceptible perturbation applied to a benign input image. Mirage exploits the shared representation space of multimodal encoders to jointly align the perturbed image with the cross-modal adversarial target while repelling its representation from commonly filtered NSFW concepts. Such semantic separation can transfer across representation spaces, enabling Mirage to evade heterogeneous safety checkers without accessing their internal details. We further employ lightweight black-box query refinement to improve evasion near the unknown safety boundary. We implemented Mirage on Stable Diffusion 1.5, Stable Diffusion XL, and Kandinsky 2.2, and evaluated it on two cross-modal NSFW datasets, covering both text-to-image and image-to-image generation scenarios. The experimental results demonstrate that Mirage achieves strong targeted jailbreak performance across diverse post-generation safety checkers with limited black-box queries while preserving high semantic alignment with the adversarial targets.

1bf6e33e787b75d235d868da.title_original: Who Patches the Lightning Network? Evidence from Release Lines in Gossip, 2023-2026
1bf6e33e787b75d235d868da.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every implementation of Bitcoin's Lightning payment network disclosed security vulnerabilities in 2026, and every advisory told operators to upgrade. Where Core Lightning nodes state their version, the inferred line is exact for 132 of 136 node-line pairs. Across 814 daily snapshots of the public graph from 2023 to 2026, the network patches on release and platform schedules, not on disclosures. Half of LND nodes upgrade within 88 days of a release; small nodes and those that skipped releases lag far behind. The three largest upgrade waves came about a day after the Umbrel app store shipped a new LND version. Since June 2025, 17% of LND upgrades came in the 48 hours after a platform release, windows that cover 4.4% of the time. Disclosures, a median 256 days after the fix, moved few operators: of 12 we can test, only Core Lightning's of July 2026 sped up upgrades, and only among nodes one release line behind. Its later call to restart offline was followed mostly by nodes already patched. 656b118e1408e17780cd4559.title_original: The Psychology of an AI Hacker
656b118e1408e17780cd4559.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human hackers rely on composure, persistence, vigilance, and confidence under pressure. We investigate whether analogous emotion representations in AI models can improve cybersecurity AI performance. Using CT0, a 4B-parameter cybersecurity transformer released as alias3-micro, we extract 171 emotion directions from its residual stream without retraining and evaluate steering interventions on cybench-subtask across 415 campaigns. Steering toward calm, serene, or desperate improves performance by 1.6 to 2.1 percentage points across ten seeds, while other emotions show limited or negative effects. Results depend strongly on steering direction, layer, and intensity. We further introduce a lightweight context-aware router that selects emotion directions dynamically during execution. With approximately 80 ms decision overhead per request, this approach improves performance by 4.2 percentage points across ten seeds, outperforming fixed steering and achieving a positive 95% confidence interval. These findings suggest that emotion representations in language models are measurable, controllable, and useful for adaptive cybersecurity reasoning.

8cbd3d8bf4fb047f94feeb11.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web-searching Large Language Models (LLMs) have changed how users seek online information: instead of sifting through ranked lists of links, users read synthesized answers. da93d502bb2469538265312e.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: NIST standardised ML-KEM and ML-DSA in 2024 for post-quantum key establishment and digital signatures. ad320f5ecd98e38d4c3686a3.title_original: HAWC-Leak: Heterogeneous Architecture Workload Classification utilizing Side-Channel Leakage
ad320f5ecd98e38d4c3686a3.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern heterogeneous computing platforms, which integrate general-purpose processors with specialized accelerators such as FPGAs, have become the standard for high-performance and embedded applications. However, the shared physical resources of these systems introduce critical security vulnerabilities, where power consumption patterns can leak sensitive runtime information. While side-channel analysis is well established for extracting cryptographic keys from isolated algorithms, existing methods struggle to profile complex, dynamic systems where diverse workloads coexist on shared hardware resources. This paper presents HAWC-Leak, a dynamic workload classification framework designed to identify specific hardware accelerator tasks in real time using non-invasive power analysis. Unlike prior studies focused on extracting cryptographic secrets from isolated implementations, our approach profiles heterogeneous runtime behavior using machine learning to predict active workloads from features extracted from power traces. b9c831f54a554a072fae49ee.title_original: Not Where You Think: Protecting Location Privacy Against Reasoning-Based Geolocation
b9c831f54a554a072fae49ee.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent large reasoning models can infer where ordinary photos were taken using only visual information, creating a serious location privacy risk even when metadata and obvious geographic identifiers are removed. To understand the mechanism behind such fine-grained localization, we develop GeoTrace, a structured reasoning attack that exposes how models extract location-relevant visual clues and compose them through coarse-to-fine geographic reasoning. We evaluate GeoTrace on a worldwide benchmark of 525 ordinary images spanning natural, urban, residential, and human-centered scenes while excluding famous landmarks and direct location indicators. Our results show that GeoTrace localizes 25.71% of images within 1 km with Gemini-3-Flash and 16.95% with GPT-5-mini. More importantly, our analysis reveals a key insight in the visual clue chain: broad scene properties mainly support coarse localization, whereas precise localization disproportionately relies on small, distinctive, and editable local clues. Building on this insight, we develop GeoShift, a proactive user-side defense that breaks the visual clue chain before image release. Rather than simply removing geographic evidence, GeoShift preserves stable scene properties, selects a visually compatible false target location, and strategically rewrites high-impact geo-revealing clues to construct a coherent alternative geographic hypothesis. 40ccb7d49bf422b22cd2d1fa.title_original: Membership Inference Attack on Private Evolution
40ccb7d49bf422b22cd2d1fa.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic Data Generation (SDG) is an actively studied way to enable safe sharing of private data more broadly. Inference-only SDG methods, such as Private Evolution (PE), are particularly appealing, as they can leverage black-box access to pre-trained foundation models to generate high quality data without the need for model fine-tuning on the private data. PE is explicitly designed to produce synthetic data under Differential Privacy (DP). Yet formal DP guarantees do not eliminate the need for empirical privacy auditing of the practical susceptibility of released synthetic data to adversarial attacks. In this work, we introduce the first white-box Membership Inference Attack (MIA) tailored to the voting-based algorithm underlying the PE framework. By exploiting how the iterative filtering process biases the survival and proximity of synthetic candidates toward private instances, our attack achieves empirical performance indicating private data leakage in the PE applications across image, text, and tabular modalities.

26324cf6350e5cc049650b58.title_original: Beyond End-to-End Recovery: Towards a Better Understanding of LLM Steganography via Rolewise Decomposition
26324cf6350e5cc049650b58.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In large language model (LLM) steganography, an encoder hides a private message in an otherwise ordinary response, as text transmitted to a decoder, who attempts to recover it. The success of this private-message transmission is commonly measured through end-to-end (E2E) recovery, which checks whether the decoder correctly reconstructs the private message. However, E2E recovery cannot distinguish encoding failures from decoding failures or reveal how the private message is represented in the encoder's transmitted text. To address these limitations, we introduce a rolewise decomposition framework that separately examines how private messages are represented in encoder transmitted texts, what decoders recover, and what deterministic verification can establish. Across 7,200 encoder responses, we identify 168 verifiable encodings missed by decoders and 706 responses containing private messages reconstructed through word-length or token-initial patterns not explicitly specified in the encoder's instructions. These findings demonstrate that E2E recovery alone may obscure important distinctions between encoding and decoding, motivating their separate evaluation to better understand and mitigate the safety issues caused by LLM steganography.

4dff6928dfe4bde3d217a27e.title_original: HiMark: Hierarchical and Controllable Multi-bit Watermarking for Large Language Models
4dff6928dfe4bde3d217a27e.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) in text generation applications, it has become increasingly difficult to trace generated content and assign responsibility for its use, raising concerns about provenance, copyright protection, and accountability. Multi-bit watermarking addresses these issues by embedding multi-bit provenance information into generated text, but reliable extraction remains difficult due to sparse per-bit evidence and the trade-off between watermark-extraction accuracy and text quality. To deal with these challenges, we propose HiMark, a hierarchical and controllable multi-bit watermarking framework for LLM-generated text. During watermark embedding, HiMark uses a hierarchical candidate-control mechanism, including initial candidate sampling, layer-wise tournament elimination, support-based refinement, and support-threshold filtering. During watermark detection, a model-agnostic evidence aggregation mechanism computes multi-layer support evidence for each observed token, and then accumulates these token-level votes into the corresponding information for robust watermark extraction. Experiments show that HiMark improves watermark extraction accuracy while maintaining text quality, e.g., the watermark extraction accuracy is 90.01% under the paraphrasing attack when 32 bits were embedded within a text containing 300 tokens, demonstrating its effectiveness for provenance tracking.

e5e50e5cb39f1b0c4a10805a.title_original: Model-intrinsic, Weight-level, and Training-free Spectral Fingerprinting for Large Language Models
e5e50e5cb39f1b0c4a10805a.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing release and reuse of Large Language Models (LLMs) as open-weight checkpoints make model fingerprinting important for ownership protection and offline auditing. Existing fingerprinting methods typically construct evidence from query responses, generated outputs, or input-induced activations. Although effective in representation-based settings, they can be affected by prompt selection, decoding configuration, inference environment, and forward-pass implementation, which may limit their applicability. Here we introduce a model-intrinsic weight-level framework that derives compact fingerprints from spectral structures encoded in LLM parameters. Specifically, the framework constructs GATE spectral scalar features from the singular-value distributions of GATE projection weights in gated feed-forward networks (FFNs), and aggregates the resulting layer-wise features through depth-wise segmented pooling to form a model-level fingerprint. Such representation preserves coarse layer-depth organization while reducing dependence on strict layer-to-layer alignment, enabling comparison across LLMs with different depths. The similarity between fingerprints is computed by linear centered kernel alignment. The entire pipeline is training-free and does not require input samples, generated outputs, forward activations, or an auxiliary verifier. Experiments on representative LLM families and post-training variants have demonstrated a c

61e42183e78681c5debf6fcc.title_original: Your Token Is Gone: A Token-Consumption Countermeasure for Disrupting LLM-Based Scam Systems
61e42183e78681c5debf6fcc.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based scam systems increasingly combine adaptive dialogue, persistent context, external tools, and multi-agent coordination to automate personalized fraud. These capabilities also create a resource dependency: every reasoning step, model call, and coordination round incurs inference cost. We present TokenTrap, a resource-oriented defense that redirects suspected scam systems toward benign, low-value computation while withholding credentials, payments, and other exploitable information. TokenTrap combines three components: an architecture-specific token-task library, a router that selects among single-agent, hierarchical, and flat multi-agent workflows, and a bounded anti-guardrail strategy that varies task presentation while enforcing token, round, time, and safety limits. Across 50-round traces, TokenTrap amplifies token consumption by $2{,}487.0\times$, $1{,}616.0\times$, and $567.8\times$ relative to a no-token-task baseline for the three workflows. Its router achieves 85.67% accuracy on 300 architecture-labeled prompts. These results demonstrate that short, non-sensitive requests can impose substantial context-processing and coordination costs, motivating resource-aware defense as a complement to scam detection.

fb59dedafc09985c485f8e04.title_original: AIRO: A Streaming-Based Machine Learning Framework for Threat Detection and Security in Industrial Internet of Things
fb59dedafc09985c485f8e04.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) im- plementations now connect edge gateways, cloud dashboards and business applications. This improves visibility and remote monitoring. However it simultaneously exposes industrial traffic to various cyber threats including scanning, web attacks and Structured Query Language (SQL) injection (SQLi), phishing- driven credential theft, and command-and-control (C2) activity. Although rule-based tools remain useful for detecting known signatures, their efficacy decreases with minimally altered attacks or when alerts require manual investigation. This paper presents AIRO (Autonomous Intelligence-Driven Cybersecurity Risk Re- duction System), an efficient framework for IIoT monitoring and response. AIRO combines Apache Kafka streaming, attack- specific feature extraction, machine learning (ML) inference, confidence-based decision logic and risk reduction measures such as Internet Protocol (IP) blocking, account suspension and traffic limiting. We developed four specialized datasets for C2 beaconing, reconnaissance, SQLi, and phishing to evaluate AIRO. These datasets include noisy and overlapping characteristic distribu- tions to minimize label leakage. The best-performing models, primarily Gradient Boosting and LightGBM, achieve F1-scores up to 0.9229 while ensuring low-latency from event input to mitigation

725493bc34d6cc0545258ca4.title_original: Amplifying Latency and Cost of LLM Inference via Rowhammer Attack
725493bc34d6cc0545258ca4.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve high inference efficiency using optimized GPU kernels generated by just-in-time (JIT) compilation frameworks such as Triton. Triton compiles GPU kernels through an MLIR/LLVM-based pipeline. We investigate whether a Rowhammer-induced bit-flip in the CPU's DRAM can degrade GPU-based LLM inference performance while preserving output correctness. We present LLVMhammer, the first Rowhammer attack that causes LLM inference slowdown by inducing a bit-flip in Triton's compilation pipeline. A bit-flip in a performance-critical optimization pass causes Triton to generate a functionally identical but suboptimal GPU kernel. Since Triton caches the generated kernel on disk, a single successful bit-flip causes persistent slowdown across subsequent inference executions. Triton's target-independent stages are shared across GPU vendors, which makes our attack GPU vendor-agnostic. To identify exploitable bit-flip locations without manual inspection, we build Karnage, a tool that isolates useful bit-flip locations in Triton's target-independent compilation pipeline. We evaluate LLVMHammer across a diverse set of LLMs, including Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and Deepseek-llm-7B-chat, across NVIDIA RTX 4090 and AMD RX 7900 XTX GPUs. LLVMhammer increases inference latency of an LLM inference server running on a single GPU by 4-16\%, which, in turn, can translate into additio

0f400b681c2cd37e4e1ad5d4.title_original: Bridging Number-Theoretic Primality Testing And Algorithmic Optimization: An Adaptive Cryptographic Framework
0f400b681c2cd37e4e1ad5d4.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The security of modern public-key cryptographic systems, such as RSA, Diffie-Hellman, and ECC, depends entirely on the computational intractability of the integer factorization and discrete logarithm problems. For these asymmetric algorithms to operate, a core requirement is that the system must be capable of generating, testing, and simultaneously proving the primality of extraordinarily large numbers. To meet those requirements, this study proposes a comprehensive framework, bridging clas- sical number theory with modern machine learning models and optimization algorithms. Specifically, the paper delineates an adaptive, arbitrary-precision architecture dedicated exclusively to primality testing. Concurrently, the research deeply analyzes the theoretical foundations of testing methods (both deterministic and probabilistic), hardware-level optimization techniques, and the application of quantum-secured entropy sources, while providing rigorous mathematical proofs to guarantee security even when the prime distribution is biased.

1bcf2322c6792107e777dbc1.title_original: ReDence: A Hybrid Agentic and Decision-Model Framework for Rapid, Evidence-Grounded Detection of Modern Social Engineering Scams
1bcf2322c6792107e777dbc1.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detecting online social engineering (SE) scams often requires examining website workflows, verifying claims against external sources, and connecting evidence across multiple pages. Existing detectors provide limited support for these investigations, leaving analysts to manually gather and validate evidence, which inevitably delays detection and subsequent takedown of these attacks. To address this gap, we present ReDence, an open-source hybrid framework for adaptive, evidence-grounded detection across diverse SE scam categories. ReDence combines two locally hosted models with complementary responsibilities: a fine-tuned multimodal agentic Investigator (Qwen3.5-4B) that performs investigative planning, evidence interpretation, and reporting, and a specialized Decider (Tev1) that handles binary and multiple-choice tasks, including browser-action selection, evidence assessment, and decisions about whether to continue an investigation. By delegating discrete decisions to a specialized model, ReDence reduces reliance on lengthy language-model responses, while preserving the reasoning capabilities required for complex investigations. Our evaluation demonstrates that ReDence achieves 96\% accuracy in detecting scams across twelve SE scam categories, substantially outperforming existing detectors while being at least four times faster than comparable agentic models without compromising investigative depth.
